findings.description: The bucket has no server-side encryption configuration. Objects, including the uploaded vendor roster, may be stored without encryption at rest.
The bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so uploaded ledger exports are not required to be encrypted at rest.
The bucket enables versioning and access logging but does not configure default server-side encryption, leaving model artifacts potentially unencrypted at rest.
The bucket does not enforce default server-side encryption, so runbook objects can be stored without encryption at rest.

No S3 public access block is configured for this bucket. A future bucket or object ACL/policy could expose its contents publicly without S3 Block Public Access serving as a defense-in-depth guardrail.
Although the bucket ACL is private, no S3 public access block is configured. Public ACLs or policies could later be added and expose ledger exports.
The bucket has no S3 public access block configuration, leaving it without a guardrail against future public bucket or object ACLs and policies.
The bucket lacks S3 Block Public Access settings, so later changes to ACLs or policies could make runbooks publicly accessible.
The log bucket lacks S3 Block Public Access settings. Its log-delivery ACL does not grant public access, but absent block-public-access guardrails allow future public ACL or policy exposure.
